deepening.title: A multiplier changes size
deepening.prompt: Predict whether {3/4} × 8, 1 × 8, and {5/4} × 8 are below, equal to, or above 8. Use one model to explain, then compute. Would the same strict comparisons work if the starting amount were 0?
deepening.answer: 6 < 8; 8 = 8; 10 > 8. With a starting amount of 0, all three products are 0, so the strict smaller/larger rule requires a positive starting amount.
deepening.worked: One fourth of 8 is 2. Three fourths gives 3 × 2 = 6; four fourths gives 8; five fourths gives 5 × 2 = 10. Compare each multiplier with 1. If the starting amount is 0, every selected fraction of that amount is still 0.

deepening.teacher_hint: Split 8 into 4 equal groups, then choose 3, 4, or 5 of those groups.
